# PatternDrawer

Drawer pattern for PLUS design system. A full-height panel at the edge of the screen, for a task that needs the page in view: the details of a row, a set of filters, a short edit. It places itself in `Blanket` at that edge, over the same blanket a modal takes. Width is a step of the screen grid (sm · md · lg: 6 · 8 · 10 columns plus the modal pad), the Modal width steps. The title, description and close button follow the Modal rules. Baked-in tokens: the overlay pair (`--ds-surface-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`), Drawer/pad 16, Drawer/stack-md 16 and Drawer/inline-sm 8, no radius. Mirrors "Pattern/Drawer" in the Figma design system file. It is a real dialog: opening it moves focus inside and Tab cycles there, Escape, the close button and a click on the blanket call `onClose`, and closing returns focus to what had it. An `inline` drawer, drawn in the page flow for docs, leaves focus where it is. It takes a stack slot from the shared overlay module (`@/lib/overlay`) alongside `Modal`: at most two stack (a drawer and the confirm it raises), a third stays closed and calls `onClose`, and opening either closes a floating sidebar. An `inline` drawer takes no slot.

Also asked as: slide-over, sheet, side sheet, off-canvas.

**Import:** `import { PatternDrawer } from '@/patterns';`

## Usage

Use a Drawer to open a panel beside the page, so a person can work on one thing while the page stays in view. It dims the page with the blanket but does not hide it.

| Task | Use |
| --- | --- |
| The details of a row, filters or a short edit, with the page in view. | A Drawer. |
| A task that blocks the page, or a short decision. | A Modal. |
| Content that belongs on the page itself. | A Section or a Card. |

### Width guidance

A Drawer takes the Modal width steps, never the page grid. The width grows with the screen, never shrinks, and the sidebar never changes it. Past `lg` the page behind it is no longer in view, and the task wants a Modal or a page of its own.

| Step | Medium 768 | Large 1024 | X-Large 1440 | Made of |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sm` | 384 | 512 | 640 | 6 screen-grid columns + 2 × 16 |
| `md` | 507 | 677 | 848 | 8 columns + 2 × 16 |
| `lg` | 629 | 843 | 1056 | 10 columns + 2 × 16 |

A Drawer is placed in the [Blanket](?path=/docs/patterns-overlays-blanket--docs) with an edge placement. The Blanket drops its pad and holds the Drawer at that edge, over the same blanket and layers a [Modal](?path=/docs/patterns-overlays-modal--docs) takes.

## Best practices

### At most two overlays. {#at-most-two-overlays}

At most two overlays: a modal or drawer, and the confirm it raises. Never two unrelated overlays, and never a third; the overlay module keeps a third closed.

Do: A drawer and the confirm it raises, stacked over it.
Don't: A modal for an unrelated task opened over a drawer.

### Keep the page in view. {#keep-the-page-in-view}

Do: A medium drawer for a form or detail.
Don't: A wide drawer that covers the page.

### Use a modal for a short decision. {#use-a-modal-for-a-short-decision}

Do: A small modal for a short decision.
Don't: A drawer for a short decision.

### Place the Drawer in a Blanket. {#place-the-drawer-in-a-blanket}

Hold the Drawer full height at a screen edge, inside a Blanket. Never put it straight on the page, and never center it: a centered layer is a Modal.

## Accessibility

- The Drawer is a dialog with `aria-modal` set to true. The title is its h1 and names it through `aria-labelledby`, and the description is linked through `aria-describedby`.
- Opening moves focus to the first control inside and traps it there. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside.
- Escape, the Close button and a click on the blanket call `onClose`, and focus returns to the control that opened it. An inner control that handles Escape keeps it.
- A body that scrolls is a tab stop, so a keyboard can reach it.
- An `inline` Drawer, drawn in the page flow for docs, sets `aria-modal` to false and leaves focus where it is.

## Parts

1. **Header.** The title, an optional description and the Close button, which shows whenever `onClose` is set.
2. **Body.** A slot that takes the height the header and footer leave, and scrolls past it.
3. **Footer** (optional). A slot pinned to the bottom edge, with actions right-aligned and the primary last.

The Drawer pads 16 on every side and stacks its parts 16 apart. It has no radius, because it meets the screen edge at the top, the bottom and its own side. Figma's custom header, `actions?`, `divider?` and `loading?` have no prop in code; `column guide?` is Figma only and never ships.

### States

A Drawer is open or closed. Closing it returns focus to what had it before it opened. Its parts have no hover, pressed or disabled states of their own; those belong to the controls in the header and footer. When focus lands on the Drawer itself, it draws the focus ring inside its edge.

### Tokens

| Token | Value | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--drawer-pad` | 16 | Pad on every side, every size. |
| `--drawer-stack-md` | 16 | Space between the header, body and footer. |
| `--drawer-inline-sm` | 8 | Space in the header row and between footer buttons. |
| `--drawer-stack-sm`, `-lg`; `--drawer-inline-md`, `-lg` | 8, 24; 16, 24 | Spacing for the content you place in the body. The Drawer does not apply them. |
| `--drawer-width-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | see Width guidance | The three width steps, the same values as the Modal's. |
| `--ds-surface-overlay`, `--ds-shadow-overlay` | overlay pair | The Drawer's fill and elevation. |
| `--heading-medium` | 20/24 | The title. |
| `--body-default`, `--ds-text-subtle` | 14/20 | The description. |
| `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` | focus ring | The ring when the Drawer itself holds focus. |
| `--ds-blanket` | 32% in Light, 60% in Dark | The fill the Blanket draws behind it. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| A short title that names what the Drawer holds: "Session details". | A title that repeats the button that opened it word for word. |
| A description only when it adds something, such as "Thursday · 4:00–5:00 PM". | A description that restates the title. |
| Name the primary action for what it does: "Save changes". | "OK" or "Submit". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `open` | bool | `true` | Whether the drawer shows. Closing it returns focus to what had it before it opened. |
| `title` | node | — | The title in the header row: the dialog's h1, at Heading/medium 20, and its name |
| `description` | node | — | One line under the title, in the subtle text color; it describes the dialog |
| `onClose` | func | — | Called by the close button, Escape and a click on the blanket; renders the close button |
| `footer` | node | — | Footer slot, pinned to the bottom edge (typically action buttons, the primary last) |
| `width` | oneOf | `'sm'` | `sm` · `md` · `lg`: 6 · 8 · 10 columns of the screen grid plus the drawer pad (384 · 507 · 629 at 768, 512 · 677 · 843 at 1024, 640 · 848 · 1056 at 1440), the Modal width steps. Grows with the screen, never shrinks, ignores the sidebar. |
| `placement` | enum | `'end'` | `end` (default) holds it at the right edge of a left-to-right page; `start` at the left. |
| `inline` | bool | `false` | Draw in the page flow at a stand-in screen, for docs and previews; focus stays where it is. |
| `screenWidth` | number | — | Inline only: the stand-in screen width (px), such as 768, 1024 or 1440. |
| `screenHeight` | number | — | Inline only: the stand-in screen height (px); the drawer runs its full height. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |
| `onKeyDown` | func | — | Runs before the drawer's own Escape and Tab handling; preventing the default on Escape keeps the drawer open. |
| `children` | node | — | Body content slot; it scrolls once it outgrows the screen |

## Variants

**`width`** — `sm` · `md` · `lg`

**`placement`** — `end` · `start`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.
